quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers to stay in the right lane to avoid a hazard ahead.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, what must you do?

options.text: Always signal, even if no other cars are visible.
Signal only if you see other traffic.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only in heavy nighttime traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if no other cars are visible.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from the curb. Make signaling a habit so you follow the law every time.

questions.question: When an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Do what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.explanation: Follow the officer's directions instead of the traffic light when an officer is directing traffic.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what should you do?

options.text: Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and let other traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means slow down and let traffic in the intersection or on the road you are entering go first.

questions.question: What should you do before turning?
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn.

questions.question: What is a sign of a drunk driver?
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include weaving, driving too fast or too slow, jerking motions, and sudden stops.

questions.question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:

options.text: Are better drivers because they are not hungry.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. This makes it hard to stay in your lane and control your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: When are seat belts most effective?

options.text: When worn by the driver only.
When passengers wear them on long drives.
When all occupants wear them on highways.
When all occupants wear them every time the car is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: When all occupants wear them every time the car is driven.
questions.explanation: Everyone in the car should wear a seat belt every time. In a crash, a person without a seat belt becomes a projectile and can hurt others in the car.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Slow down on wet or slushy roads.
Watch for standing water or puddles.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, cars take longer to stop and may skid when turning. Do not use cruise control in wet or icy conditions. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: To drive safely, you should:

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular check-ups.
Know how medicines affect your driving.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects how safely you can drive. Know your limitations and only drive when it is safe.

questions.question: Road rage and aggressive driving can be reduced by:
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, use turn signals, obey speed limits, and allow plenty of time for your trip.

questions.question: You see a driver ahead using one hand and talking to a passenger. You should:

options.text: Know that the driver is not paying full attention and is less safe.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving. If another driver seems distracted, stay far away from them because they are more likely to have an accident.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no train in sight, you must stop if:
questions.explanation: Always stop at railroad crossings if red lights flash, a gate is down, a stop sign is posted, or a flagger signals you to stop. Never try to go around crossing gates or beat a train.

questions.question: Passing another vehicle is not allowed:
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills, curves, at intersections, or at railroad crossings. These places are unsafe for passing.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than day driving because:

options.text: You cannot see as far in the dark.
You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you can see less far ahead. Always use your headlights and drive slowly enough to stop within what you can see.

questions.question: A vehicle is following you too closely. You should:

options.text: Get behind them and use your high beams.
Tap your brakes lightly, slow down, and let them pass.
Drive slowly to keep them from passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brakes lightly, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Tap your brakes lightly to warn them, then slow down to let them pass. If needed, pull over and stop to let them go by.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal early, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot whenever you change your vehicle's position. Look over your shoulder before turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Stress and strong emotions affect your driving ability. If you are worried, excited, afraid, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Stress reduces your focus on driving. It is better to wait to drive than to drive when you are emotionally upset.

questions.question: To help relieve fatigue on a long trip, it is a good idea to:

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours on long trips to rest and avoid fatigue. If you feel drowsy, pull over to a safe place and take a nap or stay at a hotel for the night.

questions.question: Pedestrians must:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing the street.
Observe and obey "Walk" and "Don't Walk" signals.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians must use crosswalks at intersections, look both ways before crossing, and follow all "Walk" and "Don't Walk" signs. Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians crossing the street.

questions.question: To change lanes you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, turn on your signal and check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and make sure no one else is entering that lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: When you need to change lanes, it is important to:

options.text: Signal your intentions ahead of the lane change.
Make sure the lane is clear before entering.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes or exiting. Give plenty of time for your signal. Before moving right or left, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot is clear.
